findings.highlight: a singer who can only sing
findings.evidenceJa: 専任ボーカル
findings.explanation: 専任 means dedicated or specialist. The line identifies the band's instrumentation problem—a dedicated vocalist, two guitarists, and a keyboardist—not a vocalist whose abilities are limited to singing.
findings.japanese:
「確かに四人いれば普通バンドは組めるけど、
それが専任ボーカルとギター二人とキーボードとなれば
全然話は別」
findings.todokanai: "Certainly, we could form a normal band with four people, but it's a different story with a singer who can only sing, two guitarists, and a keyboardist."

findings.highlight: In the majority, right?
findings.evidenceJa: メジャー指向だよねぇ
findings.explanation: メジャー指向 describes mainstream or major-label-oriented tastes. 'In the majority' is not a viable reading and leaves the proposition unintelligible.
findings.japanese: 「メジャー指向だよねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "In the majority, right?"

findings.highlight: We absolutely don't have enough people in the sound department.
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対的にパートが足りないのよ
findings.explanation: パート means musical parts here. Kazusa says their instrumentation is missing essential parts, not that a nonexistent sound department is understaffed.
findings.japanese:
「今のメンバー構成なら、
誰かがやらなくちゃならない事なの。
絶対的にパートが足りないのよ」
findings.todokanai: "With our current numbers, someone has to take on that role. We absolutely don't have enough people in the sound department."

findings.highlight: I'd like to at least finish one song before the week is done.
findings.evidenceJa: とにかくまずはドラム。少なくとも１曲目は今週中に欲しい。
findings.explanation: Kazusa specifically wants the programmed drum part for at least the first song by the end of the week. The translation turns that assignment into the much broader task of finishing an entire song.
findings.japanese:
「とにかくまずはドラム。
少なくとも１曲目は今週中に欲しい。できる？
ま、できなくてもやってもらうんだけど」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, drums first. I'd like to at least finish one song before the week is done. Can you do it? Well, do it even if you can't."

findings.highlight: You can sing the melody to the song, right?
findings.evidenceJa: キーは原曲のまんまで行けるんだよね？
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Setsuna can perform the song in its original key. The translation substitutes the unrelated question of whether she can sing its melody.
findings.japanese:
「キーは原曲のまんまで行けるんだよね？
発声練習する？」
findings.todokanai: "You can sing the melody to the song, right? Want to do voice training?"

findings.highlight: you could just stop complaining and show us something real
findings.evidenceJa: 文句を言わせない実力と、現実的なビジョンを示せば良かったのに
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that, if Takeya objected, he should have demonstrated unanswerable competence and a realistic vision. The translation replaces those two standards with an instruction to stop complaining and vaguely show 'something real.'
findings.japanese:
「不満があるならさ、文句を言わせない実力と、
現実的なビジョンを示せば良かったのに。
そしたら喜んで従ったよ？　『部長代理』」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't like it, you could just stop complaining and show us something real. Then I'll be happy to oblige, Mister Vice President."

findings.highlight: But in return, I want you to promise me something.
findings.evidenceJa: その代わり、信じさせてもらうからな
findings.explanation: Haruki is declaring that in exchange he will trust Kazusa to take care of everything that remains. He is not asking Kazusa to make a promise; the translation changes both the speech act and who assumes the trust.
findings.japanese:
「ああ約束する。
もう学園祭まではギターのことしか考えない。
その代わり、信じさせてもらうからな」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, I promise. I won't think about anything else but the guitar until the school festival. But in return, I want you to promise me something."

findings.highlight: we've regained that teacher-student relationship
findings.evidenceJa: あの時の主従関係を取り戻した
findings.explanation: 主従関係 is a master-servant relationship. Recasting it as teacher-student deletes Haruki's comic political-status metaphor and the self-abasing dependence he has just accepted.
findings.japanese:
今日やっと、あの時の主従関係を取り戻した。
だからもう、心配することはやめよう。
findings.todokanai: And today, finally, we've regained that teacher-student relationship, so there's no more need to worry now.

findings.highlight: our usual unenergetic conversation
findings.evidenceJa: いつもよりちょっと元気のない会話
findings.explanation: The conversation is a little less lively than usual. The translation instead characterizes their conversations as habitually lifeless, reversing the explicit comparison and changing the relationship baseline.
findings.japanese:
いつものように、真っ暗な道を三人で歩き、
駅で一人減って電車に乗り込んだ俺たちは、
いつもよりちょっと元気のない会話を交わした。
findings.todokanai: After the three of us walked down the dark streets together, and after the two of us got on the train, we engaged in our usual unenergetic conversation.

findings.highlight: The guitar head laid on top of me when I woke up on the floor last night.
findings.evidenceJa: ギターがベッドの上で毛布にくるまれてた
findings.explanation: The guitar was on the bed, wrapped in a blanket, while Haruki woke on the floor. The translation invents a guitar head lying on Haruki and loses the visual joke about how Kazusa treated him versus the instrument.
findings.japanese:
昨夜、俺が床の上で目覚めたとき、
ギターがベッドの上で毛布にくるまれてたっけ。
findings.todokanai: The guitar head laid on top of me when I woke up on the floor last night.

findings.highlight: There are days when I don't have to play at all
findings.evidenceJa: 一日中弾かなくてもいい日がこんなにあるなんて
findings.explanation: Kazusa marvels that there are so many days when she does not have to play all day long. The translation says there are days when she does not have to play at all, reversing the scope of the relief.
findings.japanese:
「ほんと、今は天国。
一日中弾かなくてもいい日がこんなにあるなんて」
findings.todokanai: "It's really paradise right now. There are days when I don't have to play at all…"

findings.highlight: when someone wants to change the subject
findings.evidenceJa: その転調に合わせられるくらいには、俺の人生、練習は重ねてきたつもりだ
findings.explanation: 転調 literally means musical modulation and is applied to Kazusa's conversational change of key; 合わせる sustains the musical metaphor while also meaning to adapt or play along. The translation conveys only a topic change and drops the recreatable music joke.
findings.japanese:
その転調に合わせられるくらいには、
俺の人生、練習は重ねてきたつもりだ。
findings.todokanai: I've gained enough experience throughout my life to know when to play along when someone wants to change the subject.

findings.highlight: we took a step forward with our preparations for the performance, but we're still short on time
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとだけ前進しそうだった俺のステージは、最終的には『時間切れ』という無難な結論になった
findings.explanation: Haruki's own 'stage'—both his chance to join the rehearsal and his relational opening—seemed about to advance but ended when time literally ran out at the station. The translation turns this into general progress on festival preparations plus an ongoing lack of time.
findings.japanese:
結局、ちょっとだけ前進しそうだった俺のステージは、
最終的には『時間切れ』という無難な結論になった。
findings.todokanai: In the end, it seems like we took a step forward with our preparations for the performance, but we're still short on time.

findings.highlight: I thought that I wouldn't be capable of making such an impossible assumption
findings.evidenceJa: そういう、あり得ない仮定しか、想像できなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki could imagine only the impossible hypothesis that Kazusa was inviting him home. The translation says he thought himself incapable of making that hypothesis, reversing the construction.
findings.japanese:
そういう、あり得ない仮定しか、
想像できなかったけど…
findings.todokanai: I thought that I wouldn't be capable of making such an impossible assumption, but…

findings.highlight: I saw a white room around 40 square meters large.
findings.evidenceJa: そこにはピアノを始め、沢山の楽器が転がっていた
findings.explanation: The line explicitly reveals a piano and many other instruments scattered through the room. The translation omits the entire clause, deleting the content that establishes it as a private music studio.
findings.japanese:
冬馬がその地下室の電源をつけると、
二十畳くらいの広めの白い部屋があり、
そこにはピアノを始め、沢山の楽器が転がっていた。
findings.todokanai: And when Touma turned on the lights, I saw a white room around 40 square meters large.

findings.highlight: a microphone dangling from the ceiling of a small room, closed off by glass windows
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の天井からぶら下がっている高そうなマイクと、部屋の奥にある、ガラスで仕切られた狭い部屋
findings.explanation: The source names two separate features: an expensive microphone hanging from the main room's ceiling and a narrow glass-partitioned room at the back. The translation collapses them into a microphone hanging inside the glass room.
findings.japanese:
けれど何よりも俺の目を点にしたのは、
部屋の天井からぶら下がっている高そうなマイクと、
部屋の奥にある、ガラスで仕切られた狭い部屋。
findings.todokanai: But what caught my eye the most was a microphone dangling from the ceiling of a small room, closed off by glass windows.

findings.highlight: In fact, perhaps I've been pushing my luck all day today, and it's simply that she has grown more tolerant to it.
findings.evidenceJa:
そもそも、今までと同じように、
実は今でも踏み込むだけ踏み込んでて、
ただ向こうの許容範囲が広がっただけかもしれないけど。
findings.explanation: 今までと同じように becomes 'all day today,' narrowing a recurring pattern to one day.
findings.japanese:
そもそも、今までと同じように、
実は今でも踏み込むだけ踏み込んでて、
ただ向こうの許容範囲が広がっただけかもしれないけど。
findings.todokanai: In fact, perhaps I've been pushing my luck all day today, and it's simply that she has grown more tolerant to it.

findings.highlight: the vivid image of what lies underneath is still fresh in my…
findings.evidenceJa: その制服に包まれた内部をつぶさにイメージできる今の状態では
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, although Kazusa looks as usual, he can now picture in detail what the uniform contains. The English terminates at 'my…' and never supplies the grammatical or semantic completion before the next speaker.
findings.japanese:
しかし、いつもと全く同じ外見でも、
その制服に包まれた内部をつぶさにイメージできる
今の状態では…
findings.todokanai: But even with her usual school uniform, the vivid image of what lies underneath is still fresh in my…

findings.highlight: the incredibly sociable attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 今までの小木曽とは違いすぎるあけすけな態度
findings.explanation: あけすけ describes Setsuna's startlingly open, unguarded display of favoritism, not mere sociability. The translation changes the nature of the behavioral shift driving the surrounding rumors.
findings.japanese:
今までの小木曽とは違いすぎるあけすけな態度に、
周囲がついていけてない。
findings.todokanai: Our surroundings can't keep up with the incredibly sociable attitude that Ogiso had never shown before.

findings.highlight: With a lot of sugar.
findings.evidenceJa: 一番量の多いやつで
findings.explanation: Kazusa orders the largest available cafe au lait, not one with extra sugar. Her large sugar intake is revealed separately afterward, so this substitution also damages the timing of that character joke.
findings.japanese:
「カフェオレ。
一番量の多いやつで」
findings.todokanai: "Cafe au lait. With a lot of sugar."

findings.highlight: just how little faith did I have in us, anyway?
findings.evidenceJa: どれだけ信用がなかったんだ俺
findings.explanation: Haruki is delighted that Setsuna is so overwhelmingly happy for him, then realizes how little confidence she must have had in him—or how little credibility he had. The translation makes Haruki the one who lacked faith in the group.
findings.japanese:
これがまた、俺の予想を遥かに越えた勢いで、
こんなに心から喜んでくれることが本当に嬉しくて。
…というか、どれだけ信用がなかったんだ俺。
findings.todokanai: From the bottom of my heart, I feel so happy that we've completely blown past all my predictions… Come to think of it, just how little faith did I have in us, anyway?

findings.highlight: He worked hard all by himself
findings.evidenceJa: たった一人でずっと頑張って、ちゃんと期待した通りの結果を出したんだね
findings.explanation: Setsuna is praising Haruki directly: 'You worked hard all by yourself.' The translation shifts the address into third-person narration even though Haruki is present and being spoken to.
findings.japanese:
「たった一人でずっと頑張って、
ちゃんと期待した通りの結果を出したんだね、凄いよ」
findings.todokanai: "He worked hard all by himself, and he managed to produce just the result we were hoping for! Amazing!"

findings.highlight: Touma completely takes over the conversation, noticing that I have absolutely no idea how to explain myself.
findings.evidenceJa: どうやって言い訳しようか、それもどっちに言い訳しようか逡巡した隙に、冬馬があっさり流してくれてしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki hesitates over how to explain himself and, crucially, which of the two girls he owes an explanation to; Kazusa simply lets the matter pass. The translation deletes the two-sided dilemma and invents Kazusa noticing it and taking over.
findings.japanese:
どうやって言い訳しようか、
それもどっちに言い訳しようか逡巡した隙に、
冬馬があっさり流してくれてしまった。
findings.todokanai: Touma completely takes over the conversation, noticing that I have absolutely no idea how to explain myself.

findings.highlight: Is she complimenting me?
findings.evidenceJa: 庇ってくれた、のか？
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa covered for or protected him by concealing the private tutoring. He is not asking whether she complimented him.
findings.japanese: 庇ってくれた、のか？
findings.todokanai: Is she complimenting me?

findings.highlight: evening hasn't settled in yet
findings.evidenceJa: それでも夕方のまま留まっている時間
findings.explanation: Despite shortening days, it is still lingering in evening at a little after five. The translation says evening has not arrived, reversing the scene's temporal image.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ても、まだ５時をちょっと過ぎたところ。
日に日に短くなっていく昼が、
それでも夕方のまま留まっている時間。
findings.todokanai: I look at my watch… It's a little past 5 o'clock. Even though daytime is shorter in this season, evening hasn't settled in yet.

findings.highlight: Our first rehearsal will be this Saturday and Sunday
findings.evidenceJa: この土日が第一の勝負どころだから
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls the weekend their first critical juncture or decisive push. It cannot be their first rehearsal: the script has already shown repeated rehearsals and a completed first song.
findings.japanese:
「この土日が第一の勝負どころだから、
今週末は泊まり込みで合宿ね」
findings.todokanai: "Our first rehearsal will be this Saturday and Sunday, so you'll all be staying over this weekend."

findings.highlight: whether or not we can get permission for her to stay over
findings.evidenceJa: 外泊を許可できる環境かどうか、そこに尽きるんです
findings.explanation: Haruki says the sole issue is whether the environment is safe and suitable enough for the parents to permit an overnight stay. The translation makes his criterion circular—whether permission itself can be obtained—and removes the safety argument.
findings.japanese:
「お母さん、
一生懸命かどうかはこの際問題じゃないんです。
外泊を許可できる環境かどうか、そこに尽きるんです」
findings.todokanai: "Ma'am, it's not a matter of us doing our best. It's just a matter of whether or not we can get permission for her to stay over."

findings.highlight: Start off with a strong emphasis on reason, then make an appeal to human sympathy leaving no room for any remaining opposition.
findings.evidenceJa: これぞ北原式論破術
findings.explanation: The translation omits the punchline that names this maneuver 'the Kitahara school of winning arguments.' That mock-branding is the self-parodic payoff to Haruki's description of his own technique.
findings.japanese:
最初に正論であることを強調しておきながら、
最後は人情話で誤魔化しつつ押し切る。
これぞ北原式論破術。
findings.todokanai: Start off with a strong emphasis on reason, then make an appeal to human sympathy leaving no room for any remaining opposition.

findings.highlight: that's the only thing he's good at
findings.evidenceJa: セコい詭弁に関してだけは、あたしたちは、北原の足下にも及ばない
findings.explanation: Kazusa limits the comparison: only when it comes to cheap sophistry are she and Setsuna nowhere near Haruki. The translation invents the broader insult that sophistry is the only thing Haruki is good at.
findings.japanese:
「セコい詭弁に関してだけは、
あたしたちは、北原の足下にも及ばない。
…安心して任せればいい」
findings.todokanai: "We can't hold a candle to Kitahara when it comes to sophistry, that's the only thing he's good at… Don't worry and just leave it to him."

findings.highlight: Just as I had carefully planned
findings.evidenceJa: 自分的には予定調和ながらも
findings.explanation: 予定調和 means the group's shock at the mansion is predictable or foreordained from Haruki's perspective. It does not mean he carefully planned that reaction; the translation invents personal agency.
findings.japanese:
自分的には予定調和ながらも、
冬馬家の豪華さに衝撃を受けるところから、
俺たちの合宿は幕を開けた。
findings.todokanai: Just as I had carefully planned, our stay started off with everyone being taken aback by the Touma household's extravagance.

findings.highlight: After giving it some more thought
findings.evidenceJa: 持ち時間を考えると
findings.explanation: 持ち時間 is the band's allotted stage time. They need more than one song to fill their slot, not because Kazusa has simply given the matter more thought.
findings.japanese:
「持ち時間を考えると、
レパートリー１曲じゃ全然足りないし。
あと２曲、最低でも１曲は」
findings.todokanai: "After giving it some more thought, one song isn't enough for our repertoire. We should have two more songs if possible, or at the very least one more."

findings.highlight: is not laughing anymore
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまで笑ってたカラスがもう笑顔
findings.explanation: The line moves from Kazusa laughing a moment ago to smiling now. Todokanai TL reverses that into her no longer laughing and drops the smile, changing the visible emotional progression. The Japanese also plays on a proverb about a crow's rapidly changing mood, but an English translation may recreate rather than literally retain that culturally specific verbal mechanism.
findings.japanese: さっきまで笑ってたカラスがもう笑顔…
findings.todokanai: The raven that was laughing is not laughing anymore…

findings.highlight: Even though I was busy with class rep work and always headed straight home to study in the past
findings.evidenceJa: 委員長の霍乱と言われようが、帰宅部の冷や水と言われようが
findings.explanation: Haruki adapts two stock expressions—鬼の霍乱 and 年寄りの冷や水—to his roles as class rep and homecoming-club member. The translation invents a history of being busy and going home to study, eliminating both parallel jokes.
findings.japanese:
委員長の霍乱と言われようが、
帰宅部の冷や水と言われようが、
楽しむことだけは絶対に忘れたくない。
findings.todokanai: Even though I was busy with class rep work and always headed straight home to study in the past, I won't forget to have fun this time.

findings.highlight: "My fingers are numb…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「指がつった…」
findings.explanation: 指がつった means Haruki's fingers cramped, not that they went numb.
findings.japanese: 「指がつった…」
findings.todokanai: "My fingers are numb…"

findings.highlight: Despite feeling quite awful last night
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜の段階でも余裕で壊滅中だった俺は、ちょっとばかり目眩がしたけど
findings.explanation: What was still 'devastated' the previous night was Haruki's ability to play the new song; the prospect of full-band practice makes him dizzy. The translation treats 壊滅中 as a physical illness he was suffering last night.
findings.japanese:
昨夜の段階でも余裕で壊滅中だった俺は、
ちょっとばかり目眩がしたけど、師の命令には逆らえず、
１曲目よりもかなり早い段階で全体練習が始まった。
findings.todokanai: Despite feeling quite awful last night and still feeling kind of dizzy, I can't disobey my master. We started band practice far earlier than we did for the first song.

findings.highlight: only you have nothing more to show
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬にだけは何の見せ場もないだろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki argues that Kazusa alone lacks a showcase or spotlight moment in the arrangement. 'Nothing more to show' instead implies that she has exhausted what she can demonstrate, distorting both the music proposal and its flattering motive.
findings.japanese:
「だって考えてもみろよ。
小木曽はボーカルだし、俺もソロが入る。
けど、冬馬にだけは何の見せ場もないだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, just think about it. Ogiso's the singer, and I'm also doing solos. But only you have nothing more to show, right?"

findings.highlight: I'm pridefully proclaiming this as my own personal wish
findings.evidenceJa: それは自分から望んだことだって胸を張ってるけど
findings.explanation: The omitted subject is Kazusa: she proudly maintains that being forgotten and remaining an ordinary-course underachiever is what she chose. Haruki realizes that state is only a hollow by-product of her stubbornness elsewhere. The translation makes Haruki the one proclaiming a personal wish.
findings.japanese:
それは自分から望んだことだって胸を張ってるけど、
そんなのは、別のことで意地を張ってしまったときの
虚しい副産物にしか過ぎないってわかってしまった。
findings.todokanai: Although I'm pridefully proclaiming this as my own personal wish, when I honestly think about it… it's really nothing more than the by-product of my stubbornness regarding a different matter.

findings.highlight: "Of course not…! I don't overreact that much."
findings.evidenceJa:
「やだなぁもう…！
わたし、そんなに思い込み激しくないよぉ」
findings.explanation: 思い込み激しくない becomes 'I don't overreact that much,' shifting from jumping to conclusions to emotional reaction.
findings.japanese:
「やだなぁもう…！
わたし、そんなに思い込み激しくないよぉ」
findings.todokanai: "Of course not…! I don't overreact that much."

findings.highlight: I can't chase after her
findings.evidenceJa: 追い越すことも、止めることも、そして責めることもできず、ただ同じ速度で、小木曽の後を追いかけるだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot overtake Setsuna, stop her, or reproach her; all he can do is follow at the same pace. The translation says he cannot chase her and immediately says he does follow her, replacing the first action and creating a contradiction.
findings.japanese:
わからないから、追い越すことも、止めることも、
そして責めることもできず、ただ同じ速度で、
小木曽の後を追いかけるだけ。
findings.todokanai: After all, I have no idea what she's thinking, I can't chase after her, stop her, or even counter her. I can only keep the same pace, following after Ogiso.

findings.highlight: She must have taken my ambiguous response as a negative one, and decided to ignore me.
findings.evidenceJa: 訳がわからないが故の曖昧な反応を、きっちり“悪”だと糾弾する
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly condemns Haruki's ambiguous reaction, born of incomprehension, as morally 'bad.' The translation turns that accusation into her private interpretation of his response and invents a decision to ignore him.
findings.japanese:
俺の、訳がわからないが故の曖昧な反応を、
きっちり“悪”だと糾弾する。
findings.todokanai: She must have taken my ambiguous response as a negative one, and decided to ignore me.

findings.highlight: I have absolutely no idea what could resolve this problem.
findings.evidenceJa: その心当たりも解決方法も、今の俺はまるっきり持ち合わせていない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he possesses neither a clue to the cause nor a way to fix it. The translation omits the first half of that information state, which is central to why he cannot respond to Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
そして、その心当たりも解決方法も、
今の俺はまるっきり持ち合わせていないって、こと。
findings.todokanai: And I have absolutely no idea what could resolve this problem.

findings.highlight: the unexpected attitude and reply
findings.evidenceJa: 予想通りの言葉と態度と、予想外のタイミング
findings.explanation: Setsuna's words and manner are exactly what Haruki expected; only the timing is unexpected. The translation reverses the sentence's explicit expected/unexpected contrast.
findings.japanese:
予想通りの言葉と態度と、予想外のタイミングに、
思わず声と口調が上ずってしまう。
findings.todokanai: My voice inadvertently rises at the unexpected attitude and reply.

findings.highlight: I don't want you to feel bad.
findings.evidenceJa: モヤモヤした気持ちでいるのは嫌だから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he does not want to remain in a state of unresolved unease even for an hour. The translation changes the experiencer to Setsuna and recasts his motive as protecting her feelings.
findings.japanese:
「たとえ１時間でも、
モヤモヤした気持ちでいるのは嫌だから」
findings.todokanai: "Even if it's only an hour, I don't want you to feel bad."

findings.highlight: She told me everything…
findings.evidenceJa: そしたらバレてるって
findings.explanation: Kazusa told Haruki that Setsuna had already figured out the secret. She did not disclose 'everything' to him; the translation falsely makes Kazusa the source of Setsuna's private history or feelings.
findings.japanese:
「さっき、小木曽のこと冬馬に相談した。
そしたらバレてるって…」
findings.todokanai: "I spoke with Touma about you a while ago. She told me everything…"

findings.highlight: "The closer you are to everyone, the easier it becomes to feel left out, even if it's just over small things… Kitahara-kun, did you know that?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「みんなとの距離が近ければ近いほど、
ちょっとしたことで、徹底的に仲間外れになるんだよ…
北原くん、そういうの知ってるかな？」
findings.explanation: 徹底的に仲間外れになる is weakened from being completely ostracized to feeling left out.
findings.japanese:
「みんなとの距離が近ければ近いほど、
ちょっとしたことで、徹底的に仲間外れになるんだよ…
北原くん、そういうの知ってるかな？」
findings.todokanai: "The closer you are to everyone, the easier it becomes to feel left out, even if it's just over small things… Kitahara-kun, did you know that?"

findings.highlight: they were close friends who'd stayed over at her house just a week prior to that
findings.evidenceJa: しかもそれが先週自分の家に泊まってた親友とかもう
findings.explanation: The compressed singular それ and 親友 indicate that a member of the exclusion side had been Setsuna's close friend and had stayed at her house the week before. The translation pluralizes the relationship and claims that all of 'they' were close friends who had stayed over.
findings.japanese:
小木曽から一つ一つのエピソードを聞くたびに、
少しずつ胃に重いモノが溜まってくるようだった。
しかもそれが先週自分の家に泊まってた親友とかもう…
findings.todokanai: Every single one of Ogiso's stories I hear gradually makes me feel more and more sick to the stomach. What's worse is the fact that they were close friends who'd stayed over at her house just a week prior to that.

findings.highlight: would it really be alright for me to ask Ogiso about it?
findings.evidenceJa: それでいいのか小木曽と問い質したくもなる
findings.explanation: Haruki wants to press Setsuna on whether reverting to her vulnerable former self because of him is really all right. The translation instead makes him wonder whether he has permission to ask her, reversing the modal relation.
findings.japanese:
光栄と言えばこの上なく光栄なんだけど、
それでいいのか小木曽と問い質したくもなる。
findings.todokanai: It's actually an honor among honors that I've managed to do this, but would it really be alright for me to ask Ogiso about it?

findings.highlight: From now on, you 'should' call me Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 『雪菜“が”いいからね』
findings.explanation: Setsuna has changed the earlier 雪菜でいい, 'Setsuna is fine,' to 雪菜がいい, 'Setsuna is the one I want.' The narration explicitly calls the one-particle change a power-up, but the translation repeats the same instruction and emphasizes 'should,' so the grammatical escalation no longer exists.
findings.japanese: 『雪菜“が”いいからね』
findings.todokanai: "From now on, you 'should' call me Setsuna."

findings.highlight: Everyone I got along with in my class… Until the summer holidays, anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: 仲のいいクラスだったんだよ………夏休みまではね
findings.explanation: Setsuna says theirs was a close-knit class until summer vacation. The translation misparses the class as 'everyone I got along with' and leaves the social setup as a fragment.
findings.japanese:
「中学のときはみんなそう呼んでた。
男子だって女子だって。
仲のいいクラスだったんだよ………夏休みまではね」
findings.todokanai: "Everyone called me that in middle school, both boys and girls. Everyone I got along with in my class… Until the summer holidays, anyway."
